name: Zemi (Taino Effigy)
material: Carved wood, stone, bone or cotton
powers: Houses a spirit and speaks through the behique.
description: Sculpted figures of the Taino holding a spirit, or zemi, carved from wood, stone or cotton and kept in the household or the cacique's house to give health, good harvests or answers through the behique (shaman). Spanish accounts record caciques who owned great numbers of them, and a few wooden examples survive. The word zemi names both the spirit and the object that houses it.
source: Colonial accounts and surviving Taino objects

name: Zangbeto Masquerade Costume
description: The zangbeto is a towering cone-shaped costume of plaited straw or raffia worn by the masked guardians of the night in Fon towns of Benin. Hidden inside, the performer makes the tall figure appear to spin and dance of its own accord, embodying the zangbeto spirit that patrols against witches, thieves, and wrongdoers.

name: Zanzibar Dhow
description: The dhow (jahazi) of Zanzibar is a lateen-sailed wooden vessel built on the Swahili coast for fishing, cargo, and the monsoon trade. Dhow hulls were traditionally sewn with coconut coir and caulked, and the vessels carried ivory, cloves, and mangrove poles across the Indian Ocean, tying the coast's seafaring to its maritime spirit lore.

name: Zulu Iziqu Necklace
material: Carved wood or bone blocks, fibre
description: The iziqu is the beaded or block necklace of a Zulu warrior, made of carved wooden or bone blocks strung on fibre and worn across the chest as a record of valour. Each block is said to represent an enemy killed or a brave deed, so the necklace was a personal chronicle of a man's martial history, worn at dances and ceremonies.

name: Zulu Iwisa Knobkerrie
description: The iwisa (knobkerrie) is a Zulu club with a heavy round knob and a straight handle, carried by warriors and later by chiefs and officials as a staff of rank. It was both a close-combat weapon and, in peace, a badge of authority; elaborately carved examples were made for chiefs and are still carried at ceremonies.

name: Zulu Ukhamba Beer Pot
description: The ukhamba is the fired clay beer pot of the Zulu, a round, low-necked vessel used to brew and serve utshwala, the sorghum beer central to ceremony and hospitality. Beer brewed in the ukhamba is shared at marriages, funerals, and community gatherings, and a well-made pot is prized for its strength and fine finish.
